facts.statement: Paul Rapetti installed a 16ft banner outside his Lincoln home in frustration over an 18-month wait for a decision on a disabled parking space for his wife Berta, who was terminally ill with a brain tumour.
facts.action: Installed a banner protesting the prolonged wait.
qualifications: He applied in March 2025, and the application remained undecided when the article was published.

facts.statement: Lincolnshire County Council's highways executive member said officers would review the situation and provide a recommendation so a decision could be made.
facts.actor: Lincolnshire County Council's highways executive member
facts.action: Announced a planned review and recommendation.
qualifications: The statement was not an approval or rejection of the disabled-parking-space application.

relationship.statement: The council's planned review and recommendation was a new development in the context of Rapetti's banner protest over an application that remained undecided after 18 months.

facts.statement: Trust for London, Disability Rights UK and Braw Data are collaborating on a UK-wide research project mapping funding to the disability sector.
facts.actor: Trust for London, Disability Rights UK and Braw Data
facts.action: Are collaborating on disability-sector funding research.
qualifications: The evidence supports joint collaboration and does not identify any one partner as the project's sole leader.

facts.statement: DPOs are invited to complete a 30-minute online form confirming their classification and funding sources and are offered £50 for 30 minutes.
facts.action: Are invited to provide paid research participation through an online form.
qualifications: The invitation and payment terms do not establish that funding justice has improved or that the proposed funding tool and DPO map have been delivered.

relationship.statement: The three organisations' collaborative funding-research project includes paid participation by DPOs through the specified £50, 30-minute online form.
